title: Custom yacht catering menus for dietary needs in Dubai
meta_title: Yacht Catering Dietary Menus in Dubai | myCHEF
meta_description: How dietary needs are handled in yacht catering in Dubai: briefing allergies, halal and vegetarian requests, and galley limits before departure day.
excerpt: How yacht catering menus in Dubai are customised for allergies, halal and vegan guests, and why the galley shapes the brief.
body_html:
Yes — yacht catering menus in Dubai are customised per trip, including allergies, halal requirements and vegetarian or vegan guests. What makes it different from land-based catering is the galley: limited storage, limited cooking equipment and no room for last-minute substitutions, so the dietary brief needs to reach the chef before provisioning, not on departure day. myCHEF provides the food, chef and onboard service only — never the vessel itself. Start from the yacht catering page in Dubai and send the brief below with your charter details.

What to collect per guest

Requirement typeWhat to tell the chefWhat gets planned
AllergyThe exact allergen and severitySeparate preparation and plating
Religious requirementHalal-first or equivalent, in writingWhole-menu compliance, not substitutions
PreferenceVegan, vegetarian, dislikesParallel dishes in the same menu
Medical dietWritten guidance from the guest's own professionalCooking to the written plan only

The galley is the constraint

A yacht galley usually means one cooktop, limited fridge space and no separate prep area. Menus are therefore built around fewer, better components: dishes that share base ingredients, cold courses that need no heat, and plating that works in a moving kitchen. A detailed five-course menu with twelve separate components is harder onboard than it is in a home kitchen — a good brief lets the chef propose what the galley can execute well.

A worked example (hypothetical)

Ten guests, a day charter. The brief lists one coeliac guest, a halal-first requirement for four and one vegan. The chef builds a menu where the main courses are naturally gluten-free, the halal proteins anchor the shared dishes, and the vegan guest gets a parallel course from the same ingredients rather than a separate shopping list. Provisions are bought once, with no substitutions needed at the marina.

Next step: send the guest count, trip length and dietary notes when you enquire through the yacht catering page — the brief reaching the chef before provisioning is what makes customisation possible. For related reading, see briefing a yacht chef on galley details and planning a mixed-diet menu.
